# Shopware Storefront — snippets

Every visible string is a snippet key resolved at render time. A key that does not resolve is printed literally, so a customer sees `checkout.cartHeaderProduct` instead of a heading — which is why a template rewrite has to carry its keys across.

**821 Storefront keys in 21 namespaces, 80 core keys, 2 shipped locales, 496 keys referenced by templates.**

- [Using a snippet](#using-a-snippet)

## Where snippets live

`Resources/snippet/<name>.<locale>.json`. The Storefront ships `storefront.de.json`, `storefront.en.json`. A plugin or theme adds its own file at the same path in its own bundle, and the files are merged — a key defined in several bundles resolves to the one with the highest priority, which is what makes overriding work.

The file name carries the locale, and the JSON is nested; the nesting flattens into the dotted keys used in templates, so `{"checkout": {"cartHeader": "…"}}` becomes `checkout.cartHeader`.

## Using a snippet

```twig
{{ 'checkout.cartHeaderProduct'|trans }}
{{ 'checkout.cartHeaderProduct'|trans|sw_sanitize }}
{{ 'account.orderItemCount'|trans({'%count%': items|length}) }}
<button title="{{ 'general.close'|trans|striptags }}">
```

- **`|sw_sanitize`** when the text may contain markup a shop owner edited — it strips everything unsafe and keeps basic HTML.
- **`|striptags`** in an attribute, where markup would break the HTML.
- **Placeholders** are `%name%` and are passed as a hash. A missing placeholder renders literally rather than failing.
- **In JavaScript**, pass the text in through a data attribute from the template; there is no client-side translation function.

## Overriding and adding

Create `<your-plugin>/src/Resources/snippet/storefront.en.json` with only the keys you change. The nesting must match the core file, since the merge happens per resolved key.

Snippets are also editable per sales channel in the administration, and that value wins over every file. A key that looks wrong in the shop but right in the file has usually been edited there.

Add a new key under your own namespace rather than extending a core one, so a core update cannot collide with it.

| `wishlist` | 15 | wishlist |

## Keys that come from the core bundle

Used by a Storefront template but defined in `core/Framework/Resources/snippet/`. They resolve normally; override them in a file matching the core path, not the Storefront one.

- `checkout.lineItemDeliveryDate` — Delivery period: %earliest% - %latest% — used in `storefront/component/line-item/element/delivery-date.html.twig`

## Keys referenced but not defined

Referenced by a template but present in neither the Storefront nor the core snippet file at this version. Each renders as the key itself unless a plugin or the administration supplies it. Verify before relying on one, and define it in your own snippet file if you keep the template that uses it.

- `general.requiredFields` — used in `storefront/page/account/convert.html.twig`
- `meta.xmlLang` — used in `storefront/page/content/single-cms-page.html.twig`, `storefront/page/error/error-maintenance.html.twig`
- `spatial.moveTheDeviceToStart` — used in `storefront/utilities/ar-overlay.html.twig`
- `spatial.tapToPlaceTheObject` — used in `storefront/utilities/ar-overlay.html.twig`

## Keys defined but unused

330 keys are defined but never referenced from a Storefront template. They are reached from PHP, from the administration, or from another bundle's templates — do not treat them as removable.
